lens: Adversarial mod-stability review: feasibility, update-fragility of every Harmony patch / asset-bundle / "call this internal method", unverified assumptions, and save-corruption risk from mod-created EmployeeInstance/plan state. Grounded in the on-disk decompile.
verdict: NEEDS TRIMMING + TARGETED RE-VERIFICATION before building. The core architectural call is right: Option B (mod-owned plan + state in GameInstance.modData, reuse a real game skill for the employee) is strongly supported by the decompile, and Option C is correctly rejected — SaveGameSerializationHelper confirms dual serialization (Newtonsoft TypeNameHandling.Auto + OdinSerializer binary, policy skips [Obsolete], ThrowOnErrors on serialize) and the CompatibilityFixes folder confirms aggressive purge passes (RemoveInvalidPlans, RemoveOrphanedPricingManagerPlans, CompatibilityHelper.RemoveLogisticsln/RemoveHrPlan, RemoveDuplicateEmployees, ordered UpdateGameInstanceToEA0xx lists). Phase 1 is feasible. But: (a) most of the plan's "confirmed API" method/field/string-const names are obfuscated to `n` in this decompile and are NOT actually verifiable here; (b) the delivery loop misreads the game's weekly Monday delivery cadence + lock window; (c) the Phase 2 Harmony BizMan tab is exactly as fragile as feared and is under-scoped; (d) reusing ba:skill_logisticsmanager creates a live dual-binding hazard with the vanilla LogisticsManagers HQ tab. Ship Phase 1 only, trimmed, and do the in-game verification list first.
topIssues: OBFUSCATION GAP: The decompile is only partially readable. GlobalEvents.cs, DeliveryHelper.cs, RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate, SaveGameSerializationHelper.cs and BizManBusiness.cs field layout are clear — but HrManagerPlan.cs, LogisticsManagerPlan.cs, PricingManagerPlan.cs, ScheduleHelper.cs, HrManagerHelper/LogisticsManagerHelper have EVERY method, field and even skill string-const collapsed to `n` (LogisticsManagerPlan literally does GetSkillOfEmployee(employeeId, "n")). Names the plan treats as known — ProcessStockTarget, CalculateMaxAssignableEmployees / CalculateMaxDestinations, ApplyManualPrice, ScheduleHelper.UpdateHQPlans, reg.AutoFillSchedule, PricingManagerPlan.GetSupervisedStores, LogisticsManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForEmployee, originalStorePrices — cannot be confirmed from this source. Code written against them as-if-known will not compile against the real DLL.

DELIVERY IS A WEEKLY MONDAY CYCLE, NOT A DAILY LOOP: DeliveryHelper (readable) — DeliveryDay=Monday, DeliveryHour=8, LockPeriod Sunday 20:00 -> Monday 08:00, and CanModifyContract(contractDeliveryDay) returns false during the lock period AND whenever contractDeliveryDay == next Monday. Requirement 7 and the Phase 1 goal ('from onNewDay it keeps that store stocked') are mis-framed. The mod can only usefully tune next Monday's order on Tue–Sat, before the game's own wholesale-delivery pass runs Monday 08:00. Budget accounting being weekly (WeeklyRestockBudgetCap) is consistent — but 'acts every onNewDay' is wrong.

PHASE 2 HARMONY BIZMAN TAB IS UNDER-SCOPED AND THE MOST FRAGILE THING IN THE PLAN: BizManBusiness.cs (readable) confirms `menu` and `containers` are [SerializeField] Transforms; tabs are name-matched prefab children; Awake() wires per-child button onClick; SetUpTabs() rebuilds `_tabs` as a hardcoded per-businesstype List<string> and toggles menu children by name; SetTab() does containers.Find(name) + menu.Find(name).GetComponent<TextMeshProUGUI>() + splitterIndicator.Set(); SetInitialTab() hardcodes HQ -> 'PricingManagers'; businessNameDropdown re-calls SetUpTabs. A mod tab needs a hand-built menu child (Button+TMP_Text+RectTransform matched to vanilla), a containers child, index-correct injection into a private List<string>, re-run of Awake's onClick wiring, and it reproduces bespoke UI.Elements widgets. That is 4–5 patches on private members + serialized hierarchy — breaks on essentially every game update.

DUAL-BINDING HAZARD from reusing ba:skill_logisticsmanager: GenerateCandidate (readable) switches on the skill string and returns a real `LogisticsManager` typed subclass, with side effects — adds to CandidateEmployeeInstances AND EmployeeInstancesDictionary, bumps the MyEmployees badge, fires ba:gameevent_candidatereceived. That employee then appears in the vanilla LogisticsManagers HQ tab as an assignable candidate; a player can bind it to a real LogisticsManagerPlan while the mod plan also supervises it -> two systems mutating the same store's stock. Every vanilla manager skill has its own HQ tab, so the plan's ba:skill_hrmanager fallback only reduces semantic overlap, not the mechanism.

SkillHelper.GetData(name).<field> IS CALLED UNGUARDED in the hot path — confirmed inside GenerateCandidate itself (data.secondarySkill), plus EmployeeHelper wage calc, ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox (iconImage.sprite = GetData(...).icon), HeadhunterPlan, JobDemandHelper, AiBusinessEmployeeData, RecruitmentAgencyDialog. AddressableLoader registers skills via Register<SkillData>("Skills", OnSkillDataLoaded), i.e. reloaded each city load. A Phase 3 custom skill = guaranteed NullReferenceException on the employee card / scheduler / wage calc unless a Harmony guard on GetData AND per-city-load re-injection are in place. Keep custom skill out of v1 and v2 entirely.

GameInstance.modData is confirmed real and unused (Dictionary<string,string>, sits beside [Obsolete] legacy fields at line 248) — good, this validates the sink — BUT the plan must respect: Odin serialize policy is ThrowOnErrors and skips any [Obsolete] member; the mod's own Envelope serialization must use a private permissive policy, must never mark a plan/assignment field [Obsolete] (silent data loss), and must confirm onSaveGame fires synchronously before serialize in the shipping build. The persistentDataPath fallback file must be a Phase-1 deliverable, not a 'wire it if we hit a problem'.

SAVE-SYSTEM PURGE PASSES are real and version-gated: RemoveInvalidPlans nulls employee.assignedHrlnId when the plan is gone; RemoveDuplicateEmployees does EmployeeInstances.RemoveAll by duplicate id; CompatibilityHelper.RemoveLogisticsln/RemoveHrPlan wipe plans by HQ address; per-version UpdateGameInstanceToEA0xx ordered fix lists + IntToStringMigratingDataReader with legacy type aliases run on load. A mod-created EmployeeInstance survives ONLY if its id is globally unique (GenerateCandidate handles that), it is a genuine vanilla type (it is), and it carries no dangling plan-id fields. The 3-day grace window means a save/quit during grace followed by a game update that drops the manager needs idempotent revival — test save-during-grace -> reload, and manager-reappears-with-same-id.

GlobalEvents (readable) static Actions are nulled by Init() and [RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(SubsystemRegistration)] plus onGameUnloaded. Real names confirmed: onNewDay, onNewHour, onSaveGame, onJobChange. The mod must re-subscribe on every city load and unsubscribe in OnUnloadAsync or it double-fires on save->menu->load. onJobChange takes NO arguments, so the handler must diff the whole employee list every fire.
recommendedChanges: Reframe the restock loop around the Monday delivery cycle: one 'cycle planner' that runs once per in-game week (trigger on onNewDay when day-of-week is Saturday, or an onNewHour guard), computes next Monday's per-store order within WeeklyRestockBudgetCap, respects CanModifyContract, and no-ops the rest of the week. Delete 'acts every onNewDay' language. Keep roster top-up and complaint handling on the daily tick.

Do NOT default to ba:skill_logisticsmanager. Prefer a non-manager skill that has no HQ manager tab (a common retail/operations skill) so the dual-binding mechanism disappears — the mod plan is the source of truth and the skill value still scales MaxStores. If the 'it is a manager' fiction matters, use ba:skill_hrmanager (least overlap with restocking) and add a hard guard: refuse to activate a mod plan for an employee that GetAssignedPlanForEmployee reports is bound to a vanilla plan, with a visible notification.

Cut the Phase 2 Harmony BizMan office tab from the committed roadmap. Make the ModOption.SpawnUi panel + console the permanent v1/v2 UI. Re-label the office tab an explicit 'research spike, not committed'; if pursued, prototype throwaway against the current build and gate the patch behind a game-build-number check that disables it (falls back to panel) on any unrecognized version.

Make the persistentDataPath fallback sink a Phase-1 task: keyed by save identity, with a checksum so a modData/file disagreement is detectable and logged. Wire it before the first playtest, not after a failure.

In Serialization.cs use a private permissive Odin policy for the mod's own blob (never the game's SaveGameSerializationPolicy), and add a code comment + review rule: no [Obsolete] and no property-only members on StoreManagerPlan/StoreAssignment ever.

Snapshot the FULL DeliveryContract state at assign time (enabled, repeatingOrder, wholesaleAddress, every items[] amount, nextDeliveryDay). On detach, restore verbatim only when CanModifyContract is true, else queue the restore for the next legal day.

Persist the grace-window state (planned) and make city-load revival idempotent for a manager that reappears with the same id after a game update or compat purge. Add tests for save-during-grace -> reload and manager-deleted-then-rehired.

For requirement-6 'staffing level', verify ScheduleAutoFiller.FillWithEmployees is safe to call off the Schedule UI from a mod tick (it spins a thread). If not confirmed, adjust workShifts directly on the main thread from onNewDay and defer ScheduleAutoFiller to Phase 3.
Drop price-policy writes and training budgets from all v1/v2 wording (already Phase 3) and note they depend on the obfuscated PricingManagerPlan price-write path which is currently unverifiable.

Add a load-time self-check: log the game build number, reflection-probe every method/field the mod binds, and if any critical binding is missing, refuse to activate and send the player a phone message — so a game patch degrades to 'mod dormant + player told' instead of NREs during a save.
mustVerifyInGameFirst: Runtime-dump the de-obfuscated signatures of the whole manager-plan surface (reflection/Harmony against the shipping assembly): HrManagerPlan, LogisticsManagerPlan + destination type, PricingManagerPlan, HrManagerHelper, LogisticsManagerHelper, ScheduleHelper, EmployeeHelper, RecruitmentHelper, DeliveryHelper, BuildingHelper, Contact, Notifications, InstanceBehavior<UIs>.fullMenu.bizMan. Confirm every method/field/string-const the plan names exists with that name and shape — the decompile collapses them all to `n`.

Prove GameInstance.modData round-trips a ~10–50KB string through BOTH save paths: save, force Odin binary, reload, assert equality; repeat forcing JSON. This is the persistence linchpin and the plan flags it as an open question.

Verify the DeliveryContract edit path: on a Tue–Sat in-game day, take an EXISTING player contract, flip enabled/repeatingOrder and change an items[].amount, save/reload, advance to Monday 08:00, confirm the delivery reflects the edit and the player was billed, and confirm the game's own wholesale-delivery pass does not overwrite it. Only then test a contract created from scratch by the mod (wholesaleAddress selection is the risky part).

Confirm what 'scheduled at HQ' requires: does an HQ ship with an office-desk workstation whose suitableSkills includes the chosen manager skill, or must the player place one? Confirm the real name of EmployeeInstance.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift() and that assignedAddress == HQ is also required.

Confirm GenerateCandidate's side effects are acceptable UX (mod-spawned candidate shows in the vanilla recruitment app) and decide: v1 recruits only via the vanilla Recruitment Agency / Headhunter flow, or via a mod Recruit button.

Confirm the real LogisticsManagerHelper.GetAssignedPlanForEmployee (or equivalent) exists so the mod can detect/​warn on dual-binding, and observe what actually happens when a mod-supervised manager is also added to a vanilla LogisticsManagerPlan.
Confirm onSaveGame fires synchronously before serialization in the shipping build and that a handler mutating modData inside it lands in the written file.
Confirm the ModAPI surface the plan assumes: [ModEntryOnCityLoad], locale-folder sync, ModOption.SpawnUi, and Harmony co-existence / version with the other local mod that already bundles 0Harmony.
v1ScopeRecommendation: Ship Phase 1 only, trimmed. IN SCOPE: a real EmployeeInstance recruited through the vanilla flow on a non-manager skill (or ba:skill_hrmanager, not ba:skill_logisticsmanager), appearing in My Employees with a real wage, player-scheduled at the HQ via the vanilla Schedule tab; a mod-owned plan persisted in GameInstance.modData plus a save-identity-keyed fallback file, supervising 1–N stores with a per-store weekly restock budget cap; a once-per-delivery-cycle contract planner that tunes each store's existing repeating DeliveryContract within cap (respecting CanModifyContract and the Monday lock window) and restores the full contract snapshot on detach; full visible feedback — per-action toast (Notifications.Show, signature confirmed) + weekly Contact/TextMessage digest + TransactionInfo line items; reconcile on onJobChange plus the daily tick with a persisted 3-day grace window; UI = ModOption.SpawnUi panel + console commands. OUT OF v1 (and demote the first from the roadmap): the Harmony BizMan office tab (uncommitted spike), any custom skill, price-policy writes, training budgets, warehouse-sourced restock, drag-reorder store priority, and ScheduleAutoFiller-driven staffing (start with direct workShift edits or defer). Do not start coding until mustVerifyInGameFirst items 1–4 are done — the plan's method-name surface is largely unverifiable from the obfuscated decompile, and the delivery cadence and dual-binding findings change the design.
